metadata.name: adservice
metadata.description: Gradle-built Java gRPC service deployed from `src/adservice`; no durable persistence or downstream business-service calls.

annotations.tagline: Online Boutique Java gRPC ad service that returns context-based text ads with random fallback.
annotations.capability_sheet:
## Purpose
`adservice` is the Java gRPC ad server in Online Boutique. It serves text ads from an in-memory catalog and falls back to random ads when no context matches (`src/adservice/README.md`, `src/adservice/src/main/java/hipstershop/AdService.java`).

## Public surface (REST/GraphQL/queues)
- Exposes one unary gRPC RPC: `GetAds` on `AdService`.
- No REST routes, queues, topics, or async consumers/producers.
- Packaged with Gradle (`./gradlew installDist`) and deployed as the `adservice` Skaffold artifact (`src/adservice/README.md`, `skaffold.yaml`).

## Domain entities owned
- `AdRequest`: carries context keys.
- `AdResponse`: repeated `Ad` payload.
- `Ad`: ad copy plus `redirectUrl`.
- `adsMap`: immutable category-to-ad catalog.

## Important business rules
- If `contextKeysCount > 0`, `getAds` looks up ads for each supplied context key.
- If no context is provided or the lookup returns nothing, the service calls `getRandomAds()`.
- Random fallback returns up to `MAX_ADS_TO_SERVE` ads sampled from the same in-memory catalog.

## Persistence
- None. Ads are constructed in code in `createAdsMap()` and are not written to a database or queue.

## External dependencies
- gRPC server runtime and generated proto stubs.
- Logging/tracing instrumentation in `src/adservice/src/main/resources/log4j2.xml` and `AdService.java`.

metadata.name: cartservice
metadata.description: ASP.NET Core gRPC service with a config-selected cart store; default deployment points it at Redis.

annotations.tagline: Online Boutique gRPC shopping-cart backend with Redis, Spanner, and AlloyDB storage options
annotations.capability_sheet:
## Purpose
`cartservice` is the Online Boutique shopping-cart backend. It is a .NET 10 gRPC service (`src/cartservice/src/cartservice.csproj`) containerized with Docker (`src/cartservice/src/Dockerfile`) and deployed as `cartservice` in Kubernetes (`kubernetes-manifests/cartservice.yaml`).

## Public surface
The service exposes the `hipstershop.CartService` gRPC API defined in `src/cartservice/src/protos/Cart.proto` with `AddItem`, `GetCart`, and `EmptyCart`. `Startup.cs` maps that service plus a health-check service, and the container listens on port 7070. The root HTTP `/` route only returns a helper message telling callers to use gRPC.

## Domain entities owned
The main domain objects are `Cart`, `CartItem`, and the request messages `AddItemRequest`, `GetCartRequest`, and `EmptyCartRequest`. The cart is keyed by `user_id`; each item tracks `product_id` and `quantity`.

## Important business rules
Backend selection is config-driven in `Startup.cs`: `REDIS_ADDR` enables `RedisCartStore`; otherwise `SPANNER_PROJECT` or `SPANNER_CONNECTION_STRING` selects `SpannerCartStore`; otherwise `ALLOYDB_PRIMARY_IP` selects `AlloyDBCartStore`; otherwise the service falls back to an in-memory cache plus `RedisCartStore`. In `RedisCartStore`, a missing cart creates a new `Cart`, an existing product increments its quantity, `EmptyCartAsync` writes an empty cart, and `GetCartAsync` returns an empty cart on cache miss.

## Persistence
The default Kubernetes manifest wires `REDIS_ADDR=redis-cart:6379` and deploys the shared `redis-cart` service alongside `cartservice`. Cart data is stored as serialized protobuf bytes via `IDistributedCache`, keyed by `userId`. The project also references Spanner, Npgsql, and Secret Manager packages for alternate backend implementations.

## External dependencies
Runtime dependencies include gRPC ASP.NET Core, gRPC health checks, StackExchange Redis caching, and optional Google Cloud Spanner / AlloyDB-related packages. The service runs as a single-file, self-contained .NET container entrypoint.

domain_attributes.meaning: If non-empty, `Startup.cs` registers StackExchangeRedisCache and `RedisCartStore`; if empty, configuration falls through to the other backend branches and eventually the in-memory fallback.

If non-empty, it participates in the Spanner branch; together with `SPANNER_PROJECT` it causes `Startup.cs` to bind `SpannerCartStore`.
If non-empty and the earlier branches do not match, `Startup.cs` binds `AlloyDBCartStore`; otherwise it falls through to the in-memory fallback.
`AddItemAsync` treats a null cache lookup as a missing cart and creates a new `Cart`; `GetCartAsync` treats a null lookup as a cache miss and returns an empty cart.
When a product already exists in the cart, `AddItemAsync` increments quantity; otherwise it appends a new `CartItem`.
In development mode, `Startup.cs` enables the developer exception page; otherwise that middleware is skipped.

metadata.name: checkoutservice
metadata.description: Long-running gRPC checkout orchestrator; no local datastore or queue.

annotations.tagline: Online Boutique checkout orchestrator in Go that prices carts, charges cards, ships orders, and sends confirmations.
annotations.capability_sheet:
## Purpose
`checkoutservice` is Online Boutique's checkout orchestrator. `README.md` describes it as the service that retrieves the user's cart, prepares the order, and orchestrates payment, shipping, and email. `src/checkoutservice/main.go` wires the gRPC server and health server.

## Public surface
Exposes a gRPC `CheckoutService` with `PlaceOrder`, plus `grpc.health.v1.Health` on the same listener. The service listens on `PORT` and defaults to `5050` in `main.go`; `release/kubernetes-manifests.yaml` deploys it as a `checkoutservice` Service on port `5050`.

## Domain entities owned
No local database or queue. Request-local structures include `orderPrep`, `OrderItem`, `OrderResult`, and `Money`. Order IDs are generated with UUIDs inside `PlaceOrder`.

## Important business rules
Checkout flow is ordered: fetch cart, resolve each product, convert item and shipping prices into `userCurrency`, sum the total, charge the card, ship the order, empty the cart, then send the email confirmation. Shipping failures return `Unavailable`; email failures are logged and do not fail the order. Tracing and profiling are gated by `ENABLE_TRACING` and `ENABLE_PROFILER`.

## Persistence
None in this service. Cart state lives in `cartservice`; product data and currency conversion come from other services.

## External dependencies
Uses gRPC clients for `cartservice`, `productcatalogservice`, `currencyservice`, `shippingservice`, `paymentservice`, and `emailservice`. Optional telemetry exports OTLP traces to a collector configured by `COLLECTOR_SERVICE_ADDR`, and runtime profiling can start Google Cloud Profiler when enabled.

metadata.name: currencyservice
metadata.description: Node.js gRPC currency converter on port 7000; exposes a gRPC health check alongside the business API.

annotations.tagline: Highest-QPS Node.js gRPC currency converter with bundled rates and optional Cloud Profiler/OTLP tracing
annotations.capability_sheet:
## Purpose
`currencyservice` is the Online Boutique currency converter. It is a long-running Node.js gRPC server that converts money amounts using a bundled exchange-rate table (`src/currencyservice/data/currency_conversion.json`) and is deployed on port 7000 (`release/kubernetes-manifests.yaml`). The repository README describes it as the service that converts one money amount to another currency and notes that it uses values sourced from the European Central Bank (`README.md`).

## Public surface (REST/GraphQL/queues)
- `hipstershop.CurrencyService`: `GetSupportedCurrencies` and `Convert` (`src/currencyservice/proto/demo.proto`).
- `grpc.health.v1.Health`: `Check` (`src/currencyservice/proto/grpc/health/v1/health.proto`).
- No REST routes, queues, or topics are exposed by this unit.

## Domain entities owned
- `Money`
- `CurrencyConversionRequest`
- `GetSupportedCurrenciesResponse`
- Supported ISO 4217 currency codes such as EUR, USD, JPY, GBP, CAD, TRY, and ZAR.

## Important business rules
- `GetSupportedCurrencies` returns the keys from the bundled exchange-rate table.
- `Convert` first converts the source amount to EUR and then converts EUR to the target currency code.
- The health handler always returns `SERVING`.
- `DISABLE_PROFILER` skips Google Cloud Profiler startup; `ENABLE_TRACING=1` turns on OTLP tracing.

## Persistence
- No external database, cache, or queue.
- Exchange rates are read from the bundled JSON file `src/currencyservice/data/currency_conversion.json`.

## External dependencies
- Google Cloud Profiler via `@google-cloud/profiler`.
- Optional OTLP trace collector via `COLLECTOR_SERVICE_ADDR`.
- gRPC runtime and proto loading via `@grpc/grpc-js` and `@grpc/proto-loader`.

metadata.name: emailservice
metadata.description: Python gRPC service for mock order-confirmation email; current runtime uses DummyEmailService and does not send real mail.

annotations.tagline: Python gRPC emailservice that sends mock order-confirmation emails and health checks
annotations.capability_sheet:
## Purpose
`emailservice` is the Online Boutique mock email microservice. It is a Python gRPC server built from `src/emailservice/email_server.py` and packaged with `src/emailservice/Dockerfile`. The repo README describes it as sending users an order confirmation email (mock).

## Public surface (REST/GraphQL/queues)
The service exposes `hipstershop.EmailService.SendOrderConfirmation` over gRPC, plus the standard gRPC health service. The container listens on `PORT` default `8080`; the release manifest exposes it through a ClusterIP service on port `5000`.

## Domain entities owned
The RPC takes `SendOrderConfirmationRequest` with `email` and `order`. The `order` field is an `OrderResult` containing shipping, item, and cost details reused from checkout. The HTML body is rendered from `templates/confirmation.html`.

## Important business rules
`main` always logs that the service is starting in dummy mode and calls `start(dummy_mode = True)`. That path registers `DummyEmailService`, which only logs the request and returns `Empty`; the non-dummy mail-sending path is explicitly unimplemented. Tracing is enabled only when `ENABLE_TRACING=1`, and profiler startup is skipped when `DISABLE_PROFILER` is set.

## Persistence
No datastore, queue, or topic is owned by this unit. The runtime is stateless; it renders a template and returns gRPC responses.

## External dependencies
There is no always-on downstream service call in the deployed dummy path. The only outbound integration in code is optional OTLP gRPC trace export to `COLLECTOR_SERVICE_ADDR` when tracing is enabled.

metadata.name: frontend
metadata.description: Server-side rendered Go frontend for Online Boutique; no owned datastore; depends on other services over gRPC and one HTTP assistant backend.

annotations.tagline: Go web frontend for Online Boutique that renders shopping pages and orchestrates cart, catalog, checkout, and assistant calls
annotations.capability_sheet:
## Purpose
`src/frontend` is the Go web frontend for Online Boutique. It serves the storefront UI and routes user actions to other microservices over gRPC and HTTP (`README.md`, `src/frontend/main.go`).

## Public surface
Browser routes include `/`, `/product/{id}`, `/cart`, `/cart/checkout`, `/setCurrency`, `/assistant`, and `/bot`; the handler stack also exposes `/_healthz`, `/product-meta/{ids}`, and static assets (`src/frontend/main.go`).

## Domain entities owned
The frontend does not own a database. It owns the browser session cookie (`shop_session-id`) and view-layer state such as selected currency and platform branding (`src/frontend/middleware.go`, `src/frontend/handlers.go`).

## Important business rules
- Missing session cookies create a new UUID unless `ENABLE_SINGLE_SHARED_SESSION=true`, which reuses a fixed user id (`src/frontend/middleware.go`).
- `getCurrencies` filters the currency-service response to a whitelist of USD, EUR, CAD, JPY, GBP, and TRY (`src/frontend/rpc.go`).
- `ENV_PLATFORM` controls platform branding, with GCP autodetect via `metadata.google.internal` and fallback to `local` (`src/frontend/handlers.go`).
- Product pages can optionally fetch packaging info when the packaging service is configured (`src/frontend/handlers.go`).
- Tracing and profiling are gated by `ENABLE_TRACING=1` and `ENABLE_PROFILER=1` (`src/frontend/main.go`).

## Persistence
No local datastore, queue, or object store. Session identity lives in a cookie and request context only (`src/frontend/middleware.go`).

## External dependencies
The frontend calls productcatalog, currency, cart, recommendation, shipping, checkout, and ad services over gRPC; `/bot` proxies HTTP to `shoppingassistantservice`; tracing can export to an OTLP collector; profiling can start Google Cloud Profiler (`src/frontend/main.go`, `src/frontend/rpc.go`, `src/frontend/handlers.go`).

metadata.name: loadgenerator
metadata.description: Locust-based synthetic traffic generator that sends shopping flows to the frontend.

annotations.tagline: Locust-based frontend load generator that simulates realistic shopping flows and feature-flagged traffic spikes
annotations.capability_sheet:
## Purpose
`loadgenerator` is the synthetic traffic generator for Online Boutique. It runs as a Python/Locust workload and continuously sends realistic shopping flows to the frontend so the demo can be exercised under load ([README.md:306](README.md#L306)).

## Public surface
This unit does not expose a business API of its own. It is a load-testing worker with a Locust web UI for controlling the run and observing stats; its primary runtime target is the frontend service ([README.md:306](README.md#L306)).

## Domain entities owned
It owns no persisted business entities. Its code models user journeys such as browsing products, viewing ads and recommendations, cart interactions, checkout, and optional homepage flooding (`src/loadgenerator/locustfile.py`).

## Important business rules
The generator is designed around realistic shopping behavior rather than synthetic random traffic. A feature flag, `loadgeneratorFloodHomepage`, switches on a higher-volume homepage flood mode, and `LOCUST_BROWSER_TRAFFIC_ENABLED` toggles browser-based traffic generation (`src/loadgenerator/locustfile.py`).

## Persistence
No datastore is owned by this component. Any state is ephemeral process state within the Locust run.

## External dependencies
The workload targets `frontend` over HTTP and uses `Flagd` / OpenFeature for feature-flag evaluation. It also relies on Locust for orchestration and Playwright for browser-style traffic when enabled (`src/loadgenerator/locustfile.py`).

metadata.name: paymentservice
metadata.description: Stateless Node.js gRPC payment service. Exposes Charge plus gRPC health checks and does not own persistence.

annotations.tagline: Node.js gRPC payment microservice that validates cards and returns transaction IDs for Online Boutique.
annotations.capability_sheet:
## Purpose
`paymentservice` is the Online Boutique payment microservice. It validates mock card charges and returns a synthetic transaction ID instead of charging a real card ([README.md](/workspace/microservices-demo/README.md), [protos/demo.proto](/workspace/microservices-demo/protos/demo.proto)).

## Public surface (REST/GraphQL/queues)
gRPC only. `HipsterShopServer` registers `PaymentService.Charge` and the standard gRPC health check service ([src/paymentservice/server.js](/workspace/microservices-demo/src/paymentservice/server.js), [protos/demo.proto](/workspace/microservices-demo/protos/demo.proto)).

## Domain entities owned
`ChargeRequest`, `ChargeResponse`, `CreditCardInfo`, and `Money` are the core payloads. Successful charges return `transaction_id` ([protos/demo.proto](/workspace/microservices-demo/protos/demo.proto), [src/paymentservice/charge.js](/workspace/microservices-demo/src/paymentservice/charge.js)).

## Important business rules
Only `visa` and `mastercard` card types are accepted. Bad card numbers raise `InvalidCreditCard`, unsupported types raise `UnacceptedCreditCard`, and expired cards raise `ExpiredCreditCard` ([src/paymentservice/charge.js](/workspace/microservices-demo/src/paymentservice/charge.js)). Profiler startup is skipped when `DISABLE_PROFILER` is set, and tracing starts only when `ENABLE_TRACING == "1"` ([src/paymentservice/index.js](/workspace/microservices-demo/src/paymentservice/index.js)).

## Persistence
No datastore, cache, or queue is used in the focus path. The service is stateless and generates the transaction ID in memory ([src/paymentservice/charge.js](/workspace/microservices-demo/src/paymentservice/charge.js), [src/paymentservice/server.js](/workspace/microservices-demo/src/paymentservice/server.js)).

## External dependencies

metadata.name: productcatalogservice
metadata.description: Go gRPC service that serves the product catalog from a bundled JSON file. It supports the documented dynamic catalog reload bug and EXTRA_LATENCY request delay knob.

annotations.tagline: Go gRPC product catalog service for Online Boutique with JSON-backed search/get and dynamic reload latency controls.
annotations.capability_sheet:
## Purpose
`src/productcatalogservice` is the Online Boutique product catalog service. It serves product list, lookup, and search from a bundled JSON catalog rather than a database (`README.md`, `src/productcatalogservice/README.md`, `src/productcatalogservice/Dockerfile`).

## Public surface
`protos/demo.proto` defines the `ProductCatalogService` gRPC API with `ListProducts`, `GetProduct`, and `SearchProducts`. The container exposes port `3550` (`src/productcatalogservice/Dockerfile`).

## Domain entities owned
`Product` records with `id`, `name`, `description`, `picture`, `price_usd`, and `categories`. The catalog data lives in `products.json`.

## Important business rules
The package README documents two runtime knobs: `USR1` turns on the dynamic catalog-reloading bug so the catalog is re-read on each request, and `USR2` turns it off. `EXTRA_LATENCY` injects a per-request sleep. The same README calls out `parseCatalog` as the hot path when reloading is enabled.

## Persistence
No external datastore. The catalog file is copied into the image and served from the container filesystem (`src/productcatalogservice/Dockerfile`).

## External dependencies
No runtime outbound service calls or queues were identified for this focus unit. Build/deploy wiring is via Skaffold and Kubernetes manifests (`skaffold.yaml`, `kubernetes-manifests/kustomization.yaml`).

metadata.name: recommendationservice
metadata.description: Stateless Python gRPC service that samples up to 5 recommendations after excluding already-selected product IDs.

annotations.tagline: Online Boutique Python gRPC service that filters cart product IDs and samples 5 related products
annotations.capability_sheet:
## Purpose
`recommendationservice` is the Python gRPC microservice in Online Boutique that recommends products from cart contents. The README describes it as recommending other products based on what is in the cart. The container launches `recommendation_server.py`.

## Public surface (REST/GraphQL/queues)
- gRPC `hipstershop.RecommendationService.ListRecommendations` from `protos/demo.proto` and `src/recommendationservice/recommendation_server.py`
- gRPC health service `Check`/`Watch` registered in `src/recommendationservice/recommendation_server.py`
- Container listens on port `8080` in `src/recommendationservice/Dockerfile` and `release/kubernetes-manifests.yaml`

## Domain entities owned
- `ListRecommendationsRequest` / `ListRecommendationsResponse`
- `product_ids` request and response fields

## Important business rules
- Fails fast if `PRODUCT_CATALOG_SERVICE_ADDR` is empty.
- Fetches all products from `ProductCatalogService.ListProducts`, removes any IDs already present in the request, then randomly returns up to five remaining IDs.
- `DISABLE_PROFILER` skips profiler initialization; `ENABLE_TRACING=1` enables OTLP trace export.

## Persistence
- No database, cache, or queue. Recommendations are computed in memory from the upstream catalog response.

## External dependencies
- `ProductCatalogService` over gRPC at `PRODUCT_CATALOG_SERVICE_ADDR`.
- Optional trace export to an OTLP collector via `COLLECTOR_SERVICE_ADDR` when tracing is enabled.

metadata.name: shippingservice
metadata.description: Go gRPC service that returns mock shipping quotes and mock tracking IDs.

annotations.tagline: Go gRPC shipping service for Online Boutique that returns mock USD quotes and tracking IDs.
annotations.capability_sheet:
## Purpose
shippingservice is the Online Boutique Go microservice that calculates shipping quotes and generates mock tracking IDs. The repo README places it in the overall app as the service that gives shipping cost estimates and ships items to the given address (mock) ([README.md](/workspace/microservices-demo/README.md), [src/shippingservice/main.go](/workspace/microservices-demo/src/shippingservice/main.go)). It is packaged as a container entrypoint in [src/shippingservice/Dockerfile](/workspace/microservices-demo/src/shippingservice/Dockerfile) and deployed as a Kubernetes `Deployment` in [release/kubernetes-manifests.yaml](/workspace/microservices-demo/release/kubernetes-manifests.yaml).

## Public surface (REST/GraphQL/queues)
This unit exposes a gRPC `ShippingService` with `GetQuote` and `ShipOrder`, plus the standard gRPC health service (`Check`, `Watch`) and server reflection registration ([src/shippingservice/main.go](/workspace/microservices-demo/src/shippingservice/main.go)).

## Domain entities owned
The service owns shipping quote responses (`CostUsd`) and mock shipment identifiers (`TrackingId`). Its requests are `GetQuoteRequest` and `ShipOrderRequest`, and `ShipOrderRequest` carries the address fields used to synthesize a mock tracking identifier.

## Important business rules
`GetQuote` sums the quantities of all items in the request and returns a USD amount. `ShipOrder` concatenates street, city, and state into a `baseAddress`, then derives a tracking ID from that address. Startup behavior is controlled by `DISABLE_TRACING`, `DISABLE_PROFILER`, and `PORT`; the release manifest sets `PORT=50051` and `DISABLE_PROFILER=1` for the shipped container.

## Persistence
No database, cache, or message queue is owned or accessed by this unit.

## External dependencies
The only runtime third-party service dependency found in this unit is Google Cloud Profiler, which starts during boot when `DISABLE_PROFILER` is unset. Tracing and stats hooks exist in code but are currently stubbed out ([src/shippingservice/main.go](/workspace/microservices-demo/src/shippingservice/main.go)).

metadata.name: shoppingassistantservice
metadata.description: Flask-based assistant service deployed behind a Kubernetes Service on port 8080.

annotations.tagline: Python Flask shopping-assistant service that uses Gemini + AlloyDB RAG to suggest products for Online Boutique.
annotations.capability_sheet:
## Purpose
`shoppingassistantservice` is the Online Boutique shopping-assistant add-on. The repo’s README describes it as a new service that adds a RAG-featured AI assistant to the frontend experience and uses an AlloyDB-backed products catalog to suggest items that match home decor ([kustomize/components/shopping-assistant/README.md](kustomize/components/shopping-assistant/README.md)).

## Public surface
The deployable unit is exposed as an HTTP workload on container port `8080` behind a ClusterIP Service named `shoppingassistantservice` ([kustomize/components/shopping-assistant/shoppingassistantservice.yaml](kustomize/components/shopping-assistant/shoppingassistantservice.yaml)). The indexed source I could recover did not include the Flask route definitions, so I did not invent endpoint paths.

## Domain entities owned
The assistant works against an AlloyDB-backed product catalog, with the catalog table and database names injected at deploy time via `ALLOYDB_DATABASE_NAME` and `ALLOYDB_TABLE_NAME` ([kustomize/components/shopping-assistant/shoppingassistantservice.yaml](kustomize/components/shopping-assistant/shoppingassistantservice.yaml)). The setup docs also reference `src/productcatalogservice/products.json` as seed data for populating the AlloyDB tables ([kustomize/components/shopping-assistant/README.md](kustomize/components/shopping-assistant/README.md)).

## Important business rules
The deployment requires a Google API key, AlloyDB cluster/instance/database/table identifiers, a Secret Manager secret name, project metadata, and a workload-identity service account annotation (`ALLOYDB_USER_GSA_ID`) ([kustomize/components/shopping-assistant/shoppingassistantservice.yaml](kustomize/components/shopping-assistant/shoppingassistantservice.yaml)). The docs also say you must enable GKE/Artifact Registry, create AlloyDB infrastructure, and replace the `GOOGLE_API_KEY` placeholder before deploying ([kustomize/components/shopping-assistant/README.md](kustomize/components/shopping-assistant/README.md)).

## Persistence
Primary persistence is an AlloyDB PostgreSQL catalog accessed through `langchain-google-alloydb-pg` ([src/shoppingassistantservice/requirements.in](src/shoppingassistantservice/requirements.in)). The service also reads a Secret Manager secret for AlloyDB credentials.

## External dependencies
Runtime dependencies include Google Gemini / generative AI via `langchain-google-genai` and `GOOGLE_API_KEY`, Google Cloud Secret Manager, and AlloyDB ([src/shoppingassistantservice/requirements.in](src/shoppingassistantservice/requirements.in), [kustomize/components/shopping-assistant/shoppingassistantservice.yaml](kustomize/components/shopping-assistant/shoppingassistantservice.yaml)).
